newsitem.title: USA: Universal Electronics sees Q4, FY96 loss.
newsitem.headline: Universal Electronics sees Q4, FY96 loss.

text.p: Universal Electronics Inc said it expects to report a fourth quarter net loss of $0.17-$0.22 a share versus $0.20 net income a year ago.
For the year, it said it expects a net loss of $0.19 to $0.24 a share versus net income of $0.05 a share in 1995.

In a statement late Monday, the company said it is in negotiations to sell its U.S. retail business. The expected loss was due to profit margin erosion and shortfall in expected revenue in the U.S. retail business, it said.
The stock was off 7/8 to 4-7/8 on Nasdaq. Universal makes preprogrammed remote controls for home audio/video equipment.
It also sells proprietary technologies and products to consumer electronics makers. Its technology and European retail businesses are profitable and growing, it said.

"With the exception of our U.S. One For All business our company remains strong and profitable, earning the equivalent of $0.41 to $0.49 per share for 1996," chairman, president and chief executive David Gabrielsen said in the statement.
He said the U.S. retail business had 1996 sales of $33-$35 million but had price competition and high fixed costs.

Divesting that business "will allow us to focus on applying our excellence in infrared and radio-frequency control technologies for profitable growth, particularly within the subscription broadcasting, (original equipment manufacturer) and international retail markets," he said.

Gabrielsen said a strong balance sheet will enable growth in profitable sectors. In 1996 Universal cut inventories and eliminated short-term borrowings so at yearend total debt was about $3.3 million, he said.

Universal said its forecast does not reflect cost of goods sold nor possible restructuring charges. It said it expects $28-$30 million fourth quarter net sales versus $31 million a year ago and $98-$100 million 1996 sales versus $105 million.
